maria.s: dropped an nsys capture from the flaky repro on prod-sim-3. noticing a short-lived spike in prefix-cache misses ~step 1187 that correlates with a kernel switch. attaching link to the trace: https://perf.local/trace/1976543210
kevin: thanks — quick q: was this with the new prefetch window enabled or the old immediate-prefetch?
maria.s: new prefetch=adaptive (window=32) on xg-rt v2.1.1. single host run, batch sizes were around 12-18.
samir: I skimmed the topo: the hotspot is at a KV lookup loop that calls kv_lookup_kernel_v2 and then falls back to slow_lookup_gemm when reuse < 0.3. see nsys timeline around 0:00:12.1-12.4 for repeated kernel churn.
anita: can you paste the small stack/sample from the nsys frames? that will help decide whether it's memory stall vs kernel selection cost.
maria.s: pasted sample dump below (trimmed):
```
Frame 1: kv_lookup_kernel_v2  (GPU)  1.8ms  (60% SM)
Frame 2: dispatch_thread          (GPU)  0.6ms  (20% SM)
Frame 3: fast_gemm_q4            (GPU)  3.9ms  (75% SM)
Frame 4: slow_lookup_gemm        (GPU)  4.2ms  (low occupancy)
```
kevin: interesting — fast_gemm_q4 is usually hot, but slow_lookup_gemm shows low occupancy which smells like bad launch config or tiny seqlen/padded shapes causing kernel deopt.
perf-bot: perf alert: cache_miss_rate jumped from 6% -> 18% between 1186 and 1188 (window=60s). Possible correlation with model-seqlen shift.
samir: also note the dispatcher is launching a different kernel ID after an input length >128. Kernel selection rule currently uses avg_seqlen > 96 to prefer fast_gemm_q4, otherwise uses generic fallback. if a tiny fraction crosses threshold mid-batch we get mixed kernels in same batch.
anita: mixed kernel batches are a big source of microburst latency. solution ideas: 1) pin kernel per-batch based on max seqlen, 2) separate batches by seqlen bucket, 3) prefer single-kernel fallback during heavy reuse drop.
maria.s: ran an A/B on the same trace: forcing per-batch pin to max-seqlen reduced kernel switches but increased average latency by 6% — however cache_miss_rate dropped to 8%.
kevin: tradeoff makes sense: fewer kernel switches -> more consistent KV reuse (less eviction thrash). can we tune prefetch to be aware of kernel pinning? e.g., if pinned to fast_gemm, prefetch only the prefix ranges that align with that kernel's execution shape.
samir: yes, prefetch should be shaped by kernel_type. Implementation note: we need a small change in the scheduler to attach kernel_hints to batch descriptors. low-risk patch.
anita: also let's add a microtrace measurement to Perfetto with KV cache occupancy counters so we can see evict/insert rate alongside kernel timeline.
maria.s: created a follow-up capture with occupancy counters + forced-pinning flag. uploading link: https://perf.local/trace/1976543333 — earliest observations: eviction spikes line up exactly when mini-batches cross seqlen boundary (127->129).
kevin: actionable plan:
- short-term: gate kernel selection to per-batch max-seqlen (opt-in flag) and run 24h canary on dedicated pool
- medium: implement kernel_hints in scheduler and prefetch shaping by kernel_type
- instrumentation: add KV occupancy counters and perfetto markers for prefetch windows
- follow-up: rerun synthetic traces with seqlen noise to confirm robustness
maria.s: will draft the canary PR today. assigning to @kevin for review, and @anita for perfetto instrumentation.
anita: ack. I'll add the occupancy counters and a dashboard slice for eviction rate vs hit-rate.
samir: small nit — adjust the sampling rate in nsys to capture at least 500 frames per second for these bursts, otherwise we miss the microburst kernel swaps.
kevin: good catch. maria, can you re-run capture with --sample=500 and include the cuda kernel ids mapping?
maria.s: re-capturing now, will post results. thanks all :thumbsup:
perf-bot: deploybot: canary flagged 'kernel-pin' on pool-dedicated-3 at 2026-03-18T14:02:10Z
kevin: once we have canary data, let's compare token-level cost and tail latency before flipping globally.
